I've thoroughly investigated the issue. The problem is clear:

- In `src/flask/logging.py`, the `create_logger` function uses `logging.getLogger("flask.app")` to get/create the logger. This means **all Flask app instances share the same single logger object**.
- When a user adds different handlers to different apps (e.g., `app1.logger.addHandler(handler1)` and `app2.logger.addHandler(handler2)`), both handlers end up on the same singleton `"flask.app"` logger, so every log message goes to all handlers.
- With `DispatcherMiddleware`, different apps handle different requests but log to the same logger, causing cross-contamination of log output.

The fix is to give each Flask app its own unique logger name (e.g., using `app.name` or similar), so that handlers added to one app's logger don't affect another app's logger.
